owner_creation.analysis: The IO_WAITING AtomicUsize owns the number of active IoWait guards, initialized at zero; each IoWait::new increments once.
owner_creation.invariant: Each live guard contributes one wait count.
limitations: IO_WAITING counts active read/open guards rather than owning their descriptors.

aliases_escapes.analysis: intio reads IO_WAITING by value to decide whether to post an interrupt; it receives no borrow of a guard or input buffer.
aliases_escapes.invariant: The count does not expose guard storage.
limitations: A positive counter does not validate the buffer of a particular waiter.

callback_targets.analysis: IoWait::drop is static Rust destructor dispatch; the IO_WAITING numeric counter stores no dynamically selected destructor or native callback.
callback_targets.invariant: Wait count cannot retain a callback context.
limitations: The notification protocol stores no per-waiter function target.

invalidation.analysis: Nested IoWait guards each contribute to IO_WAITING; dropping the inner guard leaves the outer count and its interruption state live.
invalidation.invariant: Ending an inner read does not retire its outer wait.

mutation_commit.analysis: IO_WAITING.fetch_add/fetch_sub pair guard lifetime, and only the decrement observing one clears IO_INTERRUPTED.
mutation_commit.invariant: The final guard alone clears pending interruption.

release_pair.analysis: A guard releases IO_WAITING's count contribution through Drop on Rust return; no malloc/free or descriptor-close pair belongs to this atomic.
release_pair.invariant: Guard destruction balances a previously added count.
limitations: IoWait Drop balances the count without closing the borrowed FD.

error_cleanup.analysis: Early I/O errors return through the IoWait destructor, decrementing IO_WAITING rather than jumping past cleanup.
error_cleanup.invariant: I/O errors cannot skip ordinary guard destruction.

signals_handoff.analysis: intio reads IO_WAITING atomically without borrowing a guard; count correctness still depends on paired ordinary Rust guard lifetime.
signals_handoff.invariant: Handler notification does not mutate guard ownership.
limitations: Review covers this atomic storage and its wait/interrupt protocol only; M0-SIG-004 remains open for rless_signal sentinel conversions.

src/os.rs.relationship: iread and iopen at src/os.rs:229-236 and src/os.rs:267-275 create IoWait guards; intio at src/os.rs:290-295 tests IO_WAITING before notification. The count spans active blocking calls.

finding_context.M0-SIG-004: IO_WAITING counts active guards and gates intio notification. M0-SIG-004 concerns disposition conversion at registration, independent of balancing wait counts; this counter neither stores nor validates a returned signal target.
